nodes.title: SG-10.2.4 Keyboard focus moves write to the store focus
nodes.body:
Context: BootScene.onKeyDown (game/frontend/src/phaser/BootScene.ts) moves focus with moveFocus and only emits the focusChange event on phaserToReact. The store already has focusedObjectId and setFocusedObject, and applyFocusedObject already pushes store focus into the scene. Desired behavior: Tab, Shift+Tab and arrow keys write the newly focused id to the store via setFocusedObject. Expected result: the store is the single owner of focus state. Why: avoids duplicated focus ownership between Phaser and React.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a scene with a focusable object, when Tab is pressed, then useGameStore.getState().focusedObjectId equals the id of the object now focused.
- Given focus moves with Shift+Tab or an arrow key, when the handler runs, then the store focusedObjectId equals the newly focused id.
- Given no object is focused after a move, when the handler runs, then the store focusedObjectId is null.
- Given a keyboard focus move, when the store is written, then applyFocusedObject leaves the scene focus unchanged and does not blur the focused object.


## Scope
- In scope: BootScene.onKeyDown writes store focus
- Out of scope: Backend changes
- Out of scope: Pointer hover handling
- Out of scope: New focus UI
- Preserve: focusChange and menuClose events still emitted
- Preserve: Enter, Space and Escape behavior
- Preserve: applyFocusedObject behavior
- Preserve: gameStore API


## Technical constraints
- Reuse useGameStore.setFocusedObject; do not add store fields
- Phaser 3.90 APIs only


## Definition of done
- Keyboard focus moves update the store focusedObjectId
- Existing keyboard and focus tests still pass


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Tab and arrow keys write the focused object id to the store
nodes.body:
Context: onKeyDown calls moveFocus then emits focusChange only. Desired behavior: after moveFocus, the scene calls useGameStore.getState().setFocusedObject(id) for Tab, Shift+Tab and arrow keys. Expected result: the store focusedObjectId matches the scene's focused object after every move. Why: store becomes the owner of focus.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given objects [bookshelf] and Tab pressed, when handled, then the store focusedObjectId is 'bookshelf'.
- Given Shift+Tab or ArrowLeft pressed, when handled, then setFocusedObject is called with the focused object id.
- Given the focusChange event, when a move happens, then it is still emitted with the same id.


## Scope
- In scope: onKeyDown store write
- Out of scope: Enter, Space, Escape handling
- Preserve: focusChange event payload


## Technical constraints
- Write via setFocusedObject only


## Definition of done
- Store write happens on every focus-moving key


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Store write stays consistent with scene focus and null when nothing is focused
nodes.body:
Context: the focused id is currently computed inline for the event. Desired behavior: a single private helper computes the focused id (null when none) and its result is used for both the store write and the focusChange event, so the later store-driven applyFocusedObject is a no-op. Expected result: no focus flicker or blur after a keyboard move. Why: single source of focus truth.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given no object isFocused after a move, when handled, then store focusedObjectId is null and focusChange emits id null.
- Given the store write triggers onStateChange, when applyFocusedObject runs, then the focused object's blur is not called.


## Scope
- In scope: Private helper in BootScene for the focused id
- Out of scope: Changing applyFocusedObject
- Preserve: applyFocusedObject semantics


## Technical constraints
- Keep helper private to BootScene


## Dependencies
- REQ1 Act touches the same handler


## Definition of done
- Store and event use the same computed id


## Clarifying questions
- None
